title: Towards Better Branching Policies: Leveraging the Sequential Nature of Branch-and-Bound Tree
claim: A two-stage training procedure first pretrains discriminative candidate embeddings contrastively, then trains a sequence model autoregressively over whole decision trajectories.
layout: 2 boxed panels, left-to-right; dashed red gradient-flow lines versus solid black data flow
description: The figure has two dashed rounded panels. The left panel, Step 1 Contrastive Learning, takes a state s_t=(C_t, Tree_t) and expert action a_t. These pass through an Embedding Layer to give candidate embeddings e_t. Expert embedding e_t^{a_t} is pulled toward the max-pooled embedding e_t^m (Similar) and pushed from the other candidates (Not Similar). Both feed the contrastive loss L_c in a purple box. The right panel, Step 2 Imitation Learning, takes the full B&B tree trajectory (s_0, a_0, ..., s_T). It applies an Embedding Layer, adds position IDs, and feeds the result to the Mamba sequence model. Avg pooling and softmax produce a distribution, which is compared with a_T by cross-entropy loss. Pastel yellow, green, blue, and purple boxes mark data types. Red dashed arrows show gradient flow, and a legend sits at bottom left.

abstract: The branch-and-bound (B&B) method is a dominant exact algorithm for solving Mixed-Integer Linear Programming problems (MILPs). While recent deep learning approaches have shown promise in learning branching policies using instance-independent features, they often struggle to capture the sequential decision-making nature of B&B, particularly over long horizons with complex inter-step dependencies and intra-step variable interactions. To address these challenges, we propose Mamba-Branching, a novel learning-based branching policy that leverages the Mamba architecture for efficient long-sequence modeling, enabling effective capture of temporal dynamics across B&B steps. Additionally, we introduce a contrastive learning strategy to pre-train discriminative embeddings for candidate branching variables, significantly enhancing Mamba's performance. Experimental results demonstrate that Mamba-Branching outperforms all previous neural branching policies on real-world MILP instances and achieves superior computational efficiency compared to the advanced open-source solver SCIP. The source code can be accessed at https://github.com/doctor-watson626/Mamba-Branching/.
